name: application-dividers
title: Dividers
description: Horizontal rule elements for visually separating sections of content, available in solid, gradient, and aligned label styles.
useWhen: Separating distinct content sections within a panel, form, or settings page.
Adding visual breathing room between a title label and the content beneath it.
Creating a subtle visual hierarchy break without using a heading or card boundary.
avoidWhen: The layout already uses cards, borders, or spacing to communicate section boundaries.
The divider would appear between items in a list — use list-item borders instead.
There are so many dividers on the page that they create visual noise rather than clarity.
responsiveBehavior: Dividers stretch full width of their container at all viewport sizes. Label-aligned variants maintain text alignment regardless of container width.
accessibility: Use the semantic <hr> element so screen readers can announce a thematic break between content sections.
Decorative dividers that carry no meaning should be hidden from assistive technology with role="presentation" or aria-hidden="true".
Do not use dividers as the sole method of grouping content — provide semantic structure with headings or sections.

variants.title: Base
variants.description: A simple solid horizontal rule using a single border color for clean content separation.
accessibility: Use <hr> for semantic thematic breaks; add aria-hidden="true" for purely decorative use.

variants.title: Base (Dark)
variants.description: Solid horizontal rule adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Dark divider color must provide sufficient contrast against dark backgrounds to remain visible.

variants.title: Gradient
variants.description: A centre-fading gradient rule that softens the visual weight of the divider and works well on wide layouts.
accessibility: Gradient dividers are inherently decorative and should include aria-hidden="true".

variants.title: Gradient (Dark)
variants.description: Centre-fading gradient rule adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Gradient dividers are decorative and should include aria-hidden="true".

variants.title: Left align
variants.description: A section label aligned to the left of a horizontal rule, for titling groups within a settings form or panel.
accessibility: If the label functions as a section heading, use a heading element inside the divider rather than plain text.

variants.title: Left align (Dark)
variants.description: Left-aligned label divider adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Dark label text must maintain WCAG AA contrast against the dark background.

variants.title: Left align gradient
variants.description: A left-aligned section label on a gradient rule that fades to the right for a lighter visual treatment.
accessibility: Gradient portion is decorative; label text carries the semantic meaning.

variants.title: Left align gradient (Dark)
variants.description: Left-aligned label on a gradient rule adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Label text must maintain readable contrast; gradient portion remains aria-hidden.

variants.title: Right align
variants.description: A section label aligned to the right of a horizontal rule, used to right-anchor labels in forms or panels.
accessibility: Right-aligned labels can disorient screen reader users in left-to-right layouts — prefer left alignment for primary headings.

variants.title: Right align (Dark)
variants.description: Right-aligned label divider adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Dark label text must maintain WCAG AA contrast against the dark background.

variants.title: Right align gradient
variants.description: A right-aligned section label on a gradient rule that fades to the left for a lighter visual treatment.
accessibility: Gradient portion is decorative; label text carries the semantic meaning.

variants.title: Right align gradient (Dark)
variants.description: Right-aligned label on a gradient rule adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Label text must maintain readable contrast; gradient portion remains aria-hidden.
